literature_notes: Both ledger lines (L1, L2) describe the same construct: full-length human ADAM11 with a C-terminal FLAG tag (DYKDDDDK) in pcDNA3.1. The topology landmarks place residues 756–769 in the intracellular compartment (TM ends at 755, intracellular begins at 756, protein ends at 769). A C-terminal tag appended after residue 769 is therefore intracellular, not extracellular. L2 confirms this: FLAG detection required permeabilization (total-expression readout), while surface display of the protein was measured by LGI binding without permeabilization — the FLAG tag is not accessible from the extracellular face. No ledger line reports a tag insertion at any extracellular position (N-terminus after signal-peptide cleavage, or any extracellular loop). The mature N-terminus (residue 24, T) is extracellular and would in principle accept a tag, but no ledger line supports an insertion there. Zero sites qualify.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal FLAG tag appended after residue 769 (A); topology places residues 756–769 in the intracellular compartment, and L2 confirms FLAG detection required permeabilization, consistent with an intracellular tag.
